summary: Tenant bindings stripped after backend claim whitelist filter causes 403s in private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 403s from admin/impersonation and tenant-scoped admin console calls after an ingress-side 'claim whitelist' was enabled in their private deployment. Requests originate from the customer's edge proxy -> Redwood private control plane.

Impact:
- FormaHealth admin users and service accounts unable to perform tenant-scoped admin operations (403).
- Affects multiple teams; blocks immediate admin workflows and onboarding of new service accounts.
- Occurs intermittently when requests route through an updated backend claim filter.

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) behind customer's ingress proxy.
- Region: prod us-east.
- Affected endpoints: POST /v1/admin/impersonate, GET /console/tenant/{tenant_id}/roles

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Create tenant service account and bind tenant-admin role via console/SCIM.
2) From their edge, send impersonation request: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <service-jwt>" -H "X-Forwarded-User-Claims: {\"rdw:tenant_bindings\":[\"tenant-123:admin\"]}" https://private.redwood-cp.example.com/v1/admin/impersonate
3) Observe 403. Same token via direct control-plane pod (bypassing ingress) succeeds.

Observed logs / artifacts (customer-provided):
- edge-proxy logs show: "claim-whitelist: dropped claim 'rdw:tenant_bindings' (not in allowlist) for request id=7a3f..."
- control plane audit-log: "authorization denied - no tenant_binding found" request_id=7a3f..., subject=service-account:forma-admin
- sample JWT (redacted) contains namespaced claim: "rdw:tenant_bindings": ["tenant-123:admin"]

Notes: The customer recently enabled a custom claim whitelist on their ingress (third-party WAF) to reduce header injection surface. After enabling, tenant-bound RBAC assertions are intermittently absent when requests pass through the modified path. When the customer re-routes traffic to bypass the claim whitelist, requests authenticate and authorize correctly.
comments: 2026-03-12 10:14 - Maya Chen (Support): Opened ticket after initial triage with customer. Collected edge-proxy logs and sample request/response headers.
2026-03-12 14:05 - Luis Ortega (SRE): Confirmed control-plane audit shows missing tenant binding claim in deny cases. Correlated request IDs between control-plane and customer-proxy logs.

2026-03-13 09:22 - Customer (FormaHealth): Provided WAF config snippet that enables claim whitelist: allow: ['sub','email','rdw:user_id'] (note: rdw:tenant_bindings missing). Customer says they intentionally tightened the allowlist yesterday.

2026-03-13 11:40 - Luis Ortega (SRE): Reproduced locally by applying an ingress filter that strips non-allowed claim keys. When rdw:tenant_bindings removed, RBAC evaluation fails and returns 403. Adding claim to allowlist restores behavior.
2026-03-14 08:30 - Maya Chen (Support): Notified customer of workaround and planned patch. Customer accepted temporary mitigation.
2026-03-14 12:05 - Engineering: PR opened to add defensive logging and clearer audit message when namespaced tenant claims are absent: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4889
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Ingress-level claim whitelist/filtering removes 'rdw:tenant_bindings' and other namespaced claims required by RBAC evaluation, causing downstream control-plane to see an incomplete subject assertion.
Confirmed by reproducer: local proxy filter that removes namespaced claims reproduces 403 consistently; direct bypass or allowlist change allows success.

Observed that some customers namespace tenant bindings under 'rdw:' prefix; our control-plane RBAC matcher accepts both 'tenant_bindings' and 'rdw:tenant_bindings' but only when present in incoming token or header. If the header is removed, no fallback exists and authorization fails.

Edge case: Claims were present in the JWT; however the customer's WAF removes header-representations of them when proxying. Control-plane treats header-provided claims as authoritative when X-Forwarded-User-Claims present.
resolution: Workaround applied: customer updated the ingress/WAF allowlist to include the 'rdw:tenant_bindings' claim and confirmed admin workflows restored. Engineering patch in progress to improve audit messages and to add a defensive fallback log recommending claim whitelist updates for private deployments. No code-level RBAC change deployed yet.
follow_up_actions: ENG: Merge PR that emits clearer audit messages and guidance when tenant-binding claims are absent (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4889).
DOCS: Update Private Deployment runbook to include guidance on common claim names that must be preserved by ingress/WAF ('rdw:tenant_bindings','rdw:service_roles','tenant_bindings').
SE: Reach out to customers currently on private to recommend a quick checklist before enabling claim-whitelists on their ingress (due 2026-03-20).
OPS: Add an alert that correlates control-plane 'authorization denied - no tenant_binding' messages with recent ingress config changes for faster triage.
